═══ SESSION cont: 8625 CLOSED · 1344 IS Verified +1 · A GATE THAT LANDED TODAY IS UNSATISFIABLE
    FROM ANY DEVELOPER ENV (846b), OPERATOR CHOSE TO PIN ═══

## MERGED
  1350  996a3b107f  8625: correct the per-class model env examples  (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1)

## CLOSED
  8625-7bea-67db-4cdc — 4/4 ACs ticked, each verified against the MERGED text, not by intent.

## IN FLIGHT
  1344 (129e) — Verified +1, LLM-Review -1 on bugfix-size-attestation ONLY. No code findings.
  846b pin change committed b44c6c1aa5, suite re-running, not yet pushed.

## THE HEADLINE: 129e's Verified -1 WAS NOT THE STALE-BASE TRAP
The previous handoff told me to suspect the stale-base trap. It was not that. All four CI legs
failed identically on two tests from my own new file — a genuine, reproducible host-dependence:
the bedrock leg of a provider-parametrized test builds a REAL provider (only the Agent is doubled),
and `build_bedrock_provider` resolves BOTH a region AND credentials at construction. This host has
both; CI has neither. The earlier "9863 passed" was green only because of ambient host AWS config.
Reproduced by stripping exactly what CI lacks, then fixed test-only and verified BOTH ways
(stripped env: 20 passed; this host: 20 passed). CI then went Verified +1 — 3 legs green before I
even finished reading. Suite at the amended tree: 9879 passed, 0 failed.
TWO ARMS, and the first fix attempt proved one is not enough: no region -> LLMConfigError from the
boto3 pre-check; region pinned but no creds -> botocore reaches for IMDS and trips the
network-forbidden fixture. Also: REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION does NOT help here — it is read only by
LLMConfig's env/table factory, never by direct construction. Pin the FIELD.

## 846b — THE REAL FIND, AND IT BLOCKS MORE THAN THIS EPIC
`bugfix_size_gate.py` landed on main 2026-08-03. It blocks a >150-non-test-line bug fix unless the
bug carries a plan-review op-cert whose DSSE principal is PINNED in
`.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`. Only `nava-opcert-prod` was pinned. Its key lives only in SSM,
the service that holds it has NO client in this repo (grep `opcert/jobs` finds only nginx, a
terraform output description, and unit tests), and by design it never persists what it signs
(`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: "off"`). So a large bug fix reviewed anywhere but prod had NO obtainable
attestation.
The keyring check runs BEFORE any drift classification, so a local signature can never reach the
ACCEPTED `stale-code`/`stale-head` arms — it short-circuits to `mismatch` and blocks. Verified by
reading the gate, not inferred: the message moved from "unsigned; no plan-review attestation
record" (ps1) to "mismatch; signing environment 'ade0f2ef-…' is not pinned" (ps2) after
`sign-review`, i.e. the signature IS seen and rejected purely on provenance.
NO PRECEDENT EXISTS: the only recent bug fix over the floor, e3cd (229 non-test lines), merged
2026-08-02 — ONE DAY BEFORE the gate — and carries no attestation at all. 129e is the first
change to actually meet this gate.
OPERATOR DECISION: pin this developer environment (option 2 of 4 offered). Done in b44c6c1aa5.
Era start = the tickets tip at pinning time, NOT backdated, so 129e's EXISTING cert is outside the
era and MUST BE RE-SIGNED after the pin lands. That is deliberate (story 4214 anti-backdating).

## A DOC DEFECT FOUND ONLY BY EXECUTING THE COMMANDS (8625 AC2)
All three `REBAR_LLM_<CLASS>_MODEL` examples were paired with `rebar review <id>` — an operation
that declares NO model class, so it resolves the top-level `model` and the per-class vars do
nothing to it. Executed: with FRONTIER=openai:gpt-4o the run still went to
bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8.
I got the diagnosis WRONG TWICE and both times a control corrected me — worth recording:
 1. I assumed the top-level pin was SHADOWING the class. A scratch repo with NO top-level model
    still resolved the DEFAULT, not gpt-4o. The class is not shadowed; a classless op never
    consults it.
 2. A narrow grep then said `frontier` had NO consumer at all. Searching ALL FILE TYPES found
    `gates/code-review.yaml:74  model: frontier`. The class is live via workflow STEP
    declarations, not a Python constant. (Same lesson as last session's two absence errors.)
Proof the correction is right, live: `REBAR_VERIFY_ENABLE_CODE_REVIEW=1
REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL=openai:gpt-4o rebar review-code` routed
`[code-review-base] model=openai:gpt-4o` and REACHED OpenAI — failing only on
`credit_balance_exhausted`. Routing proven; the account has no credits.

## EPIC AC EVIDENCE — 6 of 7 located or produced (recorded in full on the epic)
  AC4 NEWLY PRODUCED against a live OpenAI-compatible endpoint: composition ->
      isinstance(OpenAIProvider) True, base_url = the local endpoint, tier best_effort, and a REAL
      served request (`STUB_RECEIVED path=/v1/chat/completions auth=True`). Also reached the
      LMStudio on this host's :1234 (real third-party server) — proving routing independently.
  AC5 already on 2932 (cache_write=4017 then cache_read=4017). NOT re-run.
  AC2 was MISFILED: verify-completion-on-Bedrock is on 1aa2, not 2932 — consolidated onto 2932.
  AC6 satisfied by 129e's OWN attestation sidecar (provider/endpoint_host/tier all populated).
  AC7 satisfied by 1344's code-review sidecar: provider=bedrock, model=…opus-4-8, first_class.
  AC8 already on eb6e (alarm ARN rebar-bedrock-invoke-client-errors, read back from CloudWatch,
      forced notification with three "Successfully executed action" records).
  AC1 census: 17 of 18 children have landed commits; eb58 has ZERO and is a DECISION story whose
      code landed under 3768/b690 — recorded as vacuously satisfied, not ticked silently.

## CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR HANDOFF
129e is NOT a child of the epic. `parent_id` is null and it `blocks 061c`. The epic cannot close
until 129e closes. (The handoff's own warning applied to itself: `show` renders outgoing edges only.)

## A MISTAKE I MADE, recorded so it is not repeated
I ran `rebar review-code` and `rebar transition` INSIDE the 846b worktree while that worktree's
full suite was running. The suite reported 4 errors — "Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT" — on
four unrelated tests. Cause was my own concurrent writes (`.tickets-tracker` etc.) into REPO_ROOT,
not the change (one YAML file, 23 added lines). Re-running clean. RULE: never run a store or gate
command in a worktree whose suite is in flight; use a different worktree for store ops.

## GOTCHA CONFIRMED
`rebar list` / `rebar audit show -o json` — audit's text output is NOT valid JSON to `json.load`;
parse it as text. And `uv pip install '.[a,b]'` does NOT honour `[tool.uv] conflicts` (exits 0);
only `uv sync` does (exit 2, "incompatible with the declared conflicts"). The doc's
"not co-installable" is true of the sync/lock path.
